    // The change in value at the point from the earlier instant to the later one.
    ChangeBetween(self: ITimeVaryingScalarField2D, point: Point2D, earlier: Instant, later: Instant): Number
        => self.EvalAtTime(point, later) - self.EvalAtTime(point, earlier);

    // True where the value at the point is greater at the later instant than the
    // earlier one.
    HasIncreasedBetween(self: ITimeVaryingScalarField2D, point: Point2D, earlier: Instant, later: Instant): Boolean
        => self.EvalAtTime(point, later) > self.EvalAtTime(point, earlier);

    // True where the value at the point is smaller at the later instant than the
    // earlier one.
    HasDecreasedBetween(self: ITimeVaryingScalarField2D, point: Point2D, earlier: Instant, later: Instant): Boolean
        => self.EvalAtTime(point, later) < self.EvalAtTime(point, earlier);

        => self.EvalAtTime(point, time).Magnitude;

    //==
    // # Marching squares — cell numbering
    //
    // The 2D sibling of marching cubes (`library Voxels`), and numbered to match
    // it. Corners 0-3 are the loop (0,0), (1,0), (1,1), (0,1) in (x, y); edge e
    // joins corner e to corner (e + 1) % 4, so edge 0 is the bottom, 1 the right,
    // 2 the top and 3 the left. As in the cubes, a corner bit is set when that
    // corner is BELOW the iso level — outside the extracted region — so case 0 is
    // wholly inside and case 15 wholly outside, and both are uncut.
    // (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marching_squares)

    // The X offset (0 or 1) of cell corner c: corners 1 and 2 are the far side.
    MarchingSquaresCornerOffsetX(c: Integer): Integer
        => (c == 1 || c == 2) ? 1 : 0;

    // The Y offset (0 or 1) of cell corner c: corners 2 and 3 are the upper edge.
    MarchingSquaresCornerOffsetY(c: Integer): Integer
        => c / 2;

    //==
    // # Marching squares — the case table
    //
    // One row of four entries per configuration: up to two segments, each a pair
    // of edge indices, terminated by -1. Row c begins at c * 4. A segment runs
    // from its first edge to its second so that the extracted region — the
    // at-or-above side — lies to its LEFT, matching the counter-clockwise-outside
    // winding the tree uses everywhere else.
    // Convention: see CONVENTIONS.md - Winding.
    //
    // Cases 5 and 10 are the saddles, where all four edges are cut and the two
    // pairings are equally consistent with the corner values. They are resolved
    // SEPARATED: each cut corner gets its own segment, so the two at-or-above
    // corners of case 5 are disjoint rather than joined through the middle. The
    // alternative needs the center sample the cell does not have.
    //
    // Dispatched on `Line2D` — the type the extraction produces — following the
    // tree's constant idiom, and read as `Line2D.MarchingSquaresCaseTable`. Build
    // it ONCE per extraction and pass it down: an array literal allocates on every
    // evaluation.
    MarchingSquaresCaseTable(_: Line2D): Array<Integer>
        => [
            -1, -1, -1, -1,
             3,  0, -1, -1,
             0,  1, -1, -1,
             3,  1, -1, -1,
             1,  2, -1, -1,
             1,  0,  3,  2,
             0,  2, -1, -1,
             3,  2, -1, -1,
             2,  3, -1, -1,
             2,  0, -1, -1,
             0,  3,  2,  1,
             2,  1, -1, -1,
             1,  3, -1, -1,
             1,  0, -1, -1,
             0,  3, -1, -1,
            -1, -1, -1, -1,
        ];

    //==
    // # Marching squares — the cell kernel

    // The sampled value at corner `corner` of the cell whose minimum corner is
    // lattice node `cell`.
    MarchingSquaresCornerValue(cell: IntegerVector2, corner: Integer, valueAt: Function2<Integer, Integer, Number>): Number
        => valueAt(
            cell.X + MarchingSquaresCornerOffsetX(corner),
            cell.Y + MarchingSquaresCornerOffsetY(corner));

    // The world position of corner `corner` of the cell whose minimum corner is
    // lattice node `cell`.
    MarchingSquaresCornerPoint(cell: IntegerVector2, corner: Integer, pointAt: Function2<Integer, Integer, Point2D>): Point2D
        => pointAt(
            cell.X + MarchingSquaresCornerOffsetX(corner),
            cell.Y + MarchingSquaresCornerOffsetY(corner));

    // 1 when cell corner `corner` is below isoLevel, 0 when at or above it.
    MarchingSquaresCornerBit(cell: IntegerVector2, corner: Integer, valueAt: Function2<Integer, Integer, Number>, isoLevel: Number): Integer
        => MarchingSquaresCornerValue(cell, corner, valueAt) < isoLevel ? 1 : 0;

    // The configuration index of a cell: the four corner bits, corner c in bit c.
    MarchingSquaresCase(cell: IntegerVector2, valueAt: Function2<Integer, Integer, Number>, isoLevel: Number): Integer
        => MarchingSquaresCornerBit(cell, 0, valueAt, isoLevel)
         + MarchingSquaresCornerBit(cell, 1, valueAt, isoLevel) * 2
         + MarchingSquaresCornerBit(cell, 2, valueAt, isoLevel) * 4
         + MarchingSquaresCornerBit(cell, 3, valueAt, isoLevel) * 8;

    // How many segments the case table lists for configuration c: 0, 1 or 2.
    MarchingSquaresSegmentCount(table: Array<Integer>, c: Integer): Integer
        => table[c * 4] < 0 ? 0 : (table[c * 4 + 2] < 0 ? 1 : 2);
